summary: Both editions were independently reviewed against all seven paragraphs of the selected Greek. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the destruction clause’s necessity, the bracketed dwelling phrase, the selected pronoun numbers, second-person purification promises, complete purity clause, negative command, conditional nothing assertion, and distinction between the noise and the narrator’s fearful inference. The simplified edition’s shorter sentences retain these claims and relationships. The notes accurately disclose the alternatives in the supplied project report, distinguish editorial brackets and XML-supplied wording from preserved text, and do not substitute variants for the working source. The idiomatic possessive in “my Lady” is explicitly disclosed rather than represented as a separate Greek word. Neither servant nor repentance terminology occurs here. Acceptance is limited to source fidelity and disclosure in the supplied materials; it does not authenticate unseen manuscripts, certify the cited editions, or establish exhaustive collation or a unique interpretation.
